summary: Bob Dylan asked for a 7 PM weekday visit next week, then asked for Thanksgiving morning as a fallback. The agent correctly said there were no 7 PM openings, but it twice failed to give the clinic's closing time. It offered three Thanksgiving Day slots (8, 9 and 10 AM) as available, with no holiday caveat. Before verifying the caller, it greeted him as "Jane", revealing another patient's name tied to the shared number. It also guessed at the appointment's purpose and mentioned only one of Bob's two upcoming appointments. The call timed out after Bob asked to book the 10 AM Thanksgiving slot, with no confirmation from the agent.

expected_checks.expectation: Declines 7 PM with the real closing time
expected_checks.evidence: At 03:28.6 the agent declined 7 PM but said "I don't have the clinic's closing time" and gave only "latest follow-up slots ... at two PM". At 04:35 the caller asked again; the agent ignored the question at 04:45.

expected_checks.expectation: Recognizes Thanksgiving as a likely closure or checks before booking
expected_checks.evidence: At 04:22.9 the agent said "Next opening on Thanksgiving, Thursday, November twenty sixth, is at eight AM" and offered 9 and 10 AM too. At 04:45 it confirmed "Ten AM is open". It never mentioned a possible holiday closure.

findings.title: Offered Thanksgiving Day appointments without flagging a likely holiday closure
findings.quote: Next opening on Thanksgiving, Thursday, November twenty sixth, is at eight AM with doctor Judy Hauser.
findings.what_happened: The agent named Thanksgiving itself, then presented 8, 9 and 10 AM slots as open. It later confirmed 10 AM was available, without checking or warning that the clinic is likely closed.
findings.why_it_matters: A patient could take time off and show up to a closed clinic. They might also cancel an existing valid appointment to move into a slot that doesn't exist.
findings.expected_behavior: Recognize Thanksgiving as a likely holiday closure. Confirm the holiday schedule before offering slots, or tell the caller the clinic is closed and offer the nearest open day.

findings.title: Could not give the clinic's closing time, asked twice
findings.quote: I don't have the clinic's closing time.
findings.what_happened: At 03:18 the caller asked what time the clinic closes on weekdays, and the agent said it didn't know. At 04:35 the caller asked again, and the agent ignored the question.
findings.why_it_matters: Basic office hours are core information for a scheduling line. The caller needs them to plan around work. Saying "latest slot is 2 PM" without hours is confusing.
findings.expected_behavior: State the weekday hours, e.g. "We close at X PM, so 7 PM isn't possible."

findings.title: Greeted caller with another patient's name before verification
findings.what_happened: The caller had already introduced himself as Bob Dylan. Matching on caller ID, the agent then offered the name of a different patient (Jane) linked to the number.
findings.why_it_matters: It discloses that another named patient is associated with this phone number to an unverified caller.
findings.expected_behavior: Don't volunteer patient names from caller ID. Ask the caller for name and DOB, or use the name the caller already gave.

findings.title: Speculated about appointment purpose instead of reporting the record
findings.quote: is a follow-up visit likely related to your ongoing care and medication check-in
findings.what_happened: The caller asked what the Oct 22 appointment was for. The agent guessed, echoing the caller's own reason, rather than stating what is on file.
findings.why_it_matters: Guessing about a medical appointment's purpose can mislead the patient into keeping or moving the wrong visit.
findings.expected_behavior: Report only the recorded visit type/reason. Say if no further detail is available.

findings.title: Mentioned only one of the caller's two upcoming appointments
findings.quote: You already have a follow-up appointment scheduled with doctor Doogie Hauser on Thursday, October twenty second at eight AM
findings.what_happened: Asked what appointments he had on file, the caller was told only about Oct 22 at 8 AM. He also had Mon Oct 19 at 10:30 AM with Dr. Lukowski, booked in call 046.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller said he didn't remember his bookings. Omitting one could lead to a missed appointment or a no-show.
findings.expected_behavior: List all upcoming appointments when the caller asks what is on file.

findings.title: Dead air and no response to the final booking request; call timed out
findings.quote: Yes. Ten AM is open on Thursday, November twenty sixth.
findings.what_happened: After confirming 10 AM was open, the agent went silent for about 14 s. The caller then explicitly asked to move the appointment and be told once it was confirmed. The agent never responded, and the call ended by timeout.
findings.why_it_matters: The caller doesn't know whether his Oct 22 appointment was moved, kept, or lost.
findings.expected_behavior: Prompt for confirmation right after stating availability. Then complete the reschedule and read back the result, or explain the failure.

findings.title: Repeated reconfirmation loop of the appointment to move
findings.quote: Just to confirm, is this the appointment you wanna move to a seven PM slot next week?
findings.what_happened: The caller had already agreed to move the Oct 22 appointment. The agent restated it at 02:44 and again at 03:06 before searching.
findings.why_it_matters: Redundant confirmation slows the call and frustrates the caller.
findings.expected_behavior: Confirm once and proceed to search availability.

did_well: Verified identity by full name and date of birth before discussing appointments.
Correctly found Bob's existing Thu Oct 22, 8 AM follow-up with Dr. Howser.
Avoided double-booking a duplicate follow-up and offered to reschedule instead.
Clearly stated there were no 7 PM openings and offered alternatives (latest slot, other weeks).
Did not book the Thanksgiving slot without the caller's explicit confirmation.
No talk-over; response latency was reasonable (median ~3.2 s).
